rationale:
Evidence from iteration 4 (score 505.8, best so far): the oval now finishes on all 20 trials (mean 2.10 s, so there is time margin under 3 s). The s-bend finishes 20% of runs and the slalom 0%. Every failure is off_track at max_error about 0.06 m, the binding limit. Steering oscillation is 0.19 (oval) to 0.26 (s-bend), and it fell as kd rose from 1.0 to 1.5 and mass fell from 0.6 to 0.5. Slalom progress rose from 0.20 to 0.27. That supports the view that damping and turn agility, not raw speed, limit the bends. Speed is kept at base_speed 1.0 because the oval's time margin is small on tight sections and off-track exits dominate the score.

Changes, kept to two levers: (1) kd 1.5 to 2.0, to continue the damping trend that reduced oscillation and raised slalom progress. (2) sensor_size 0.012 to 0.016 m, so each footprint covers more tape at large lateral offsets. This should reduce the line-loss events (about 0.8 to 1.0 per run) that begin just before each off-track exit. Geometry positions, mass 0.5, wheel_track 0.10, kp 5.5, ki 0, base_speed 1.0 and line_loss last_direction are unchanged.

Expected result: s-bend finish rate above 25%, slalom progress above 0.3, line_loss_events below 0.8, and oval completion held at or near 100%. Hypotheses: H1, kd is still the limit on bends, shown by steering_oscillation falling below 0.18 with max_error staying under 0.06 on more seeds. H2, the larger footprint reduces line loss at the first sharp direction change, shown by line_loss_events falling. H3, if the signal becomes too noisy or overshoots, steering_oscillation will rise above 0.25 and control_effort will climb, meaning kd or sensor_size has gone too far. Next measurements: progress and completion_time for speed versus stability, max_error and line_loss_events for stability, steering_oscillation for damping, control_effort for gain cost, and noise_robustness for margin on held-back tracks.
